subject: Parcelium POC traffic qualification, evaluation plan, and owner commitments
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Soto <elena@parcelium.ai>, Adam Chu <adam@parcelium.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Parcelium POC traffic qualification, evaluation plan, and owner commitments

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the Parcelium team. Quick recap + my asks so we can lock the POC scope and timelines. Please review and confirm the bold items.

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary flow: user -> Parcelium API -> LLM enrichment -> store result. Estimated average payload per request: 420 tokens (prompt + expected generation).
- Peak behavior: normal steady-state ~12 RPS, concurrency 30 (clients across 3 regions), expected burst windows up to 120 RPS for ~90s during batch import periods.
- Response length distribution: 60% < 200 tokens, 30% 200-600 tokens, 10% rare long responses up to ~1,800 tokens for extended summaries.
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for short responses (<200 tokens); degraded longer responses ok for longer generations.
- Success criteria for POC: (a) sustain 12 RPS steady with p95 < 350ms, (b) survive 90s bursts to 120 RPS without >5% error rate, (c) end-to-end cost estimate within target budget (TBD).

Immediate asks / confirmations: (bold = action for Parcelium)
1) Confirm steady RPS and concurrency above (12 RPS / 30 concurrency) and whether concurrency is client-limited or server-side.
2) Confirm the max expected token length for extreme cases (we logged ~1,800 tokens). If >2,000, flag now — we need different model configs.
3) Share an example workload CSV (columns: timestamp, request_type, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, client_region) — I attached a template.
4) Agree to the POC window: 2 weeks of run + 2 days of stress probes. Proposed dates: Sep 13–Sep 26, 2027.

Our proposed evaluation plan (high level):
- Week 0 (prep): Provision dedicated test pool, upload workload matrix, smoke tests. Owner: Ben (infra).
- Week 1: Steady-state run at declared RPS to validate p95 and token accounting. Owner: Soojin + Camila.
- Week 2: Mixed traffic and burst probes, latency/cost regressions, model variant fallbacks. Owner: Ben + Camila.
- Acceptance: Meet success criteria above and sign-off by Parcelium PO (Elena) + Redwood sales eng.

Attachments: parcelium_workload_matrix.csv (template), redwood-eval-template.pdf

Next steps I can take this week:
- Ben will provision the test pool once we have the workload CSV and confirmation on max token length.
- Camila will prepare an evaluation dashboard (latency/cost tokens split) and the canary rollout plan.

Please reply with confirmations on items 1–4 and attach the CSV when ready. If the timeline above doesn't work, propose alternate dates.

Thanks,
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: Elena Soto <elena@parcelium.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Adam Chu <adam@parcelium.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Parcelium POC traffic qualification, evaluation plan, and owner commitments

Thanks Soojin — really helpful summary. Quick clarifications inline.

- Steady RPS: confirmed 12 RPS. Concurrency: client-side concurrency tends to be 20 per region (we have 3 regions) — so total ~60 concurrent connections; the ~30 figure I gave earlier was per-service thread miscommunication.
- Max length: the long summary case is actually up to ~2,200 tokens in extreme cases. We can add a guard in the client to cap at 2,000 if that would help for POC.
- We'll attach the workload CSV in the next message.

One ask from Parcelium engineering: can Redwood simulate the burst shape as 120 RPS sustained for 90s followed by a 5-minute cooldown (we want to reproduce our onboarding import spike)?

We are good with the Sep 13–26 window, but we need one change: please avoid running stress probes during our US business hours 9am–5pm PT on Sep 16 (internal all-hands).

I'll attach the CSV now.

Thanks,
Elena
Product Ops Manager
Parcelium
elena@parcelium.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Soto <elena@parcelium.ai>, Adam Chu <adam@parcelium.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Parcelium POC traffic qualification, evaluation plan, and owner commitments

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Elena. A few updates based on the higher concurrency / token ceiling and your cooldown window: 

1) Concurrency: adjust plan to expect 60 concurrent connections (20 per region). Ben will size the pool accordingly.
2) Token ceiling: we'll treat 2,200 tokens as the max. For safety, we'll provision a fallback model with a higher memory footprint for long generations; Camila will add quantization/variant notes to the eval dashboard.
3) Burst probing: yes — we can reproduce the 120 RPS x 90s spike followed by a 5-minute decay. We will schedule stress windows to avoid Sep 16 9am–5pm PT.

Attached: parcelium_workload_matrix.csv (filled sample), parcelium_poc_scope.docx, redwood-eval-template.pdf

Proposed refined timeline (milestones with owners):
- Sep 1–9: Preflight + infra provisioning (Ben) — deliverables: test pool, baseline model variant list, access creds.
- Sep 10–12: Smoke testing with small traffic, runbook rehearsal (Soojin + Camila).
- Sep 13–20: Steady-state evaluation (12 RPS, confirm p95 targets) (Camila owner for metrics).
- Sep 21–25: Burst and regression probes (Ben owner for probe orchestration).
- Sep 26: Acceptance/hand-off meeting and sign-off.

Please confirm owners and the filled CSV looks representative. If Parcelium wants an earlier start, we can accelerate provisioning this week.

Attachments (referenced):
- [Attachment: parcelium_workload_matrix.csv (text/csv)]
- [Attachment: parcelium_poc_scope.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
- [Attachment: redwood-eval-template.pdf (application/pdf)]

Next actions I will take immediately: Ben will provision a test pool once you confirm the CSV is final; Camila will share a pre-configured Grafana board and token-cost breakdown by Sep 3.

Best,
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Soto <elena@parcelium.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Parcelium POC traffic qualification, evaluation plan, and owner commitments

Looping in final infra notes — happy to own provisioning and the burst probes. Confirmed items:
- Test pool: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved for POC) + autoscaling to add 2 nodes if we detect sustained backpressure.
- Network: we will route traffic through the Redwood US-WEST cluster (closest to Parcelium) to minimize cross-region variance.
- Runbook: I'll create a lightweight runbook and incident playbook for the POC (will link in the drive).
- Contact: For on-call during probes, use my pager (ben@pager.redwood) and Camila as secondary.

One technical note: because the token ceiling is 2,200, we will prefer the slightly larger model variant for the steady run to keep tokenization overhead low. That will modestly increase cost estimates — I'll publish an initial cost delta by EOD tomorrow.

Forwarded for reference: the filled workload matrix and the sample evaluation template (see attachments in previous message).

Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.inference
